voice.factsDescription: The only numbers, years, prices and guarantees the AI may claim about the brand
voice.hooksDescription: Patterns for opening lines — '{{topic}}' is replaced automatically

facts.label: Facts about the brand
facts.hint: One fact per line. After a vertical bar you can add the source — where it can be verified.
facts.placeholder:
Baking since 1998 | chrlit.cz/about
Delivery within 24 hours in Prague
2-year warranty on everything
facts.note: What is not listed here, the AI will not state as a fact — instead of a made-up number it writes the sentence without one. You do not need to enter the live product catalogue (prices, names); the engine reads it itself.
facts.scanNothing: I found no new specific detail on the website — nothing was added.
facts.scanAdded: {count, plural, one {Added # suggestion from the website} other {Added # suggestions from the website}} — review them and delete any that do not fit. Remember to save with the button above.
facts.checkLabel: Claim check in the finished text
facts.checkHint: Neither end of the slider lets a lie through. It only changes whether the engine fixes an unsupported claim itself or sends it to you.

off.label: Off
off.detail: No check runs. The AI is still forbidden to invent details, but nobody checks it.

safe.label: Careful
safe.detail: Fixes everything it dares to, including headlines in the image. Safest — and sometimes dullest.

balanced.label: Balanced
balanced.detail: Fixes the post text; in the headline it only swaps a wrong number for the right one. An unsupported headline is left alone and flagged for you.

bold.label: Bold
bold.detail: Rewrites nothing. The text keeps its punch and every risky claim comes to you flagged for a decision.

facts.publishFlagged: Publish posts with unverified claims too
facts.publishFlaggedHint: Off: a flagged post does not publish itself and waits until you confirm or delete the claim. Once a day we e-mail you about the ones waiting.

formats.title: Post formats
formats.description: Each format is one post type (a template) you pick when generating. A “with product” format automatically attaches a real product photo. “Manual only” means the AI never picks it on its own (contests, limited drops) — only you choose it in Create.
formats.empty: No brand formats — add the first one below.
formats.removeConfirm: Really delete the format "{name}"? Already generated posts stay.
formats.name: Format name
formats.descriptionHint: WHAT the post shows and WHY it works for your brand — the AI copywriter reads this
formats.descriptionPlaceholder: Contest post: 1) like it, 2) follow our profile, 3) tag a friend in the comments — the winner gets a free product...
formats.structureHint: Content skeleton — slide outline for a carousel, scenes for a reel, text build-up for an image. Empty = the generic template for the medium
formats.structurePlaceholder: Slide 1 (COVER): question about the prize · Slide 2: contest rules · Slide 3: what you win · Slide 4: deadline + CTA
formats.visualStyleHint: How the posts should look — composition, mood, props. The AI designer follows this when designing the visual
formats.visualStylePlaceholder: Product on a bold coloured background, confetti, big numbers, energetic mood...
formats.overlayHint: How the headline sits on the image — text layout in the visual

ai.label: ✨ Let AI fill it in
ai.hint: Type a post type and the AI fills in the rest of the form — then review it and save

audience.description: Audience personas — the AI adapts tone, hooks and CTAs for each group
audience.empty: No personas defined. The AI will not personalise content.

pattern.title: Feed pattern
pattern.description: The shape your profile grid should form when someone opens your Instagram
pattern.suggestWithHandle: The AI looks at your real profile @{handle} and recommends a pattern that fits how you already look.
pattern.suggestNoHandle: Add your Instagram account in Basics and the AI will recommend a pattern based on your real profile.
pattern.noneHint: Your feed does not reveal enough for a recommendation yet — pick a pattern manually, you will see the change right away in the Feed preview.
pattern.note: The pattern only sets the layout family for each grid position — within it, posts still differ in composition, crop and typography. The setting applies to all new posts (campaign and single ones).

none.label: No pattern
none.description: Every post decides for itself. Maximum variety, no rhythm in the grid.

checkerboard.label: Checkerboard
checkerboard.description: Alternates a photo and a typographic post. In a three-column grid this forms a checkerboard — it keeps its shape even as posts thin out.

rows.label: Rows
rows.description: A full row of photos, a full row of typography. A calm, editorial feed.

columns.label: Columns
columns.description: Typographic middle column, photographic outer ones. Creates a vertical spine for the profile.

diagonal.label: Diagonal
diagonal.description: Every fourth post is a graphic accent in the brand colour — a diagonal rhythm forms in the grid.

photos.title: Where posts get their photos
photos.description: When the AI may invent a scene and when it must build on your real photo
photos.note: Upload your photos in the Brand photos section. The more there are and the better they are tagged, the more often the engine lands on a photo that fits the post. Text and logo are always drawn into the photo — what gets limited is inventing the scene, not the graphics.
photos.noPhotos: You have not uploaded a single brand photo yet — until then this setting has nothing to work with.

free.label: Free hand
free.description: The AI may invent the scene. Your photos serve as a reference for style, setting and products.

prefer-real.label: Prefer my photos
prefer-real.description: When one of your photos fits the post, the post must build on it — and this is checked. Without a fitting photo the AI fills in the scene.

only-real.label: Only my photos
only-real.description: Photos are never invented. Without a fitting photo of yours, the post goes to typography or graphics.

subtitles.title: Subtitles in reels
subtitles.description: The look of the subtitles burned into the video. Applies to new reels; on a finished reel the style can be switched in the post detail (no credits)

pop.label: Highlight
pop.description: Bigger type and the word being spoken in the brand colour. Today’s reel standard — the default.

classic.label: Classic
classic.description: White text with an outline and a subtle backdrop. Readable on anything, does not overpower the image.

cards.label: Cards
cards.description: Large type in a solid box, a few words at a time. Holds attention even without sound.

minimal.label: Minimal
minimal.description: Just a thin outline, no backdrop. Least intrusive, but gets lost on a bright scene.

subtitles.positionHint: Vertically within Instagram’s safe zone — bottom above the UI bar, centre, or top
subtitles.sizeHint: Bigger type = fewer words per line, cards change faster
subtitles.allowSilentNote: For visual subjects (food, interior, makeover) the scriptwriter can then choose text cards and music instead of a narrator. Costs the same as a reel with a voice.
subtitles.note: Instagram does not accept a subtitle track for reels — subtitles are burned into the picture. The change therefore only shows on a newly produced reel; a finished reel can be re-rendered in the post detail, free of charge (no new video is generated).

style.title: Visual style
style.description: How the AI Designer renders post images (typography, logo, video)
style.typographyHint: A free description of the type style — the AI Designer follows it (not a font file)
style.typographyPlaceholder: Bold condensed grotesk, uppercase / elegant high-contrast serif
style.logoPlacementHint: Auto = the AI picks the position and alternates it between posts

identity.videoFocusPlaceholder: Focus on interiors, first-person view, B-roll...

autoPublish.title: Auto-publishing
autoPublish.description: Posts go out on their own — on the day and hour they have in the plan. The plan sets the frequency, not this page.
autoPublish.on: On — posts go out according to the plan
autoPublish.toggleHint: Finished posts publish themselves at the scheduled time — no clicking.
autoPublish.notConnected: The account is not connected yet — the setting is saved, but publishing only starts once Instagram is connected (section above).
autoPublish.none: There is no upcoming date in the plan yet.
autoPublish.counts: {armed} armed · {waiting, plural, one {# waiting} other {# waiting}} for confirmation{overdue, plural, =0 {} one { · # overdue} other { · # overdue}}
autoPublish.overdueNote: Overdue dates do not move on their own — content written for a specific day should not go out a week later. Confirm or move them in the plan.

handoff.replaceNote: Applies only to an account that already exists; nobody is detached for an invite.
